To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in patients with endometrial, ovarian and breast cancer the cumulative relative risk of developing polyneoplasias is significantly higher than in the control groups and the risk increases from the age of forty to sixty.

1) in patients with primary breast cancer, the cumulative risk of developing synchronous endometrial cancer is 14 times higher than in healthy women; 2) in patients with synchronous breast and endometrial cancer the cumulative risk is 9 times higher than that in healthy women; the indices mentioned increase with age and in the first stages of cancer.
in patients with primary breast cancer the risk of developing corpus uteri cancer was increased 13.9, and in patients with primary corpus uteri - breast cancer - 9.0 times.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of the risk of polyneoplasm in patients with breast cancer, corpus uteri cancer and ovarian cancer, and the factors which increase this risk.
the cumulative risk of polyneuplasia and the methods of early diagnosis.

the cumulative relative risk of patients with primary endometrial, ovarian and breast cancer developing other cancers, the factors influencing it and the possibility of detecting them in the initial stage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
asymptomatic initial polyneoplasies in the first stage are detected more frequently in patients of primary corpus cancer than in the general female population.
the risk of polyneoplasy increases in the first stages of the primary cancer and the most important factor is the age of the patient.

the cumulative relative risk for polyneoplasias is higher in patients of primary corpus cancer than in patients of primary breast cancer and ovarian cancer, and the indices mentioned increase with age and the stage of disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the cumulative risk of polyneoplasty is 9.0-13.9 times as high as in the general population; the indices mentioned increase from 40 to 60 years and in the 1.st stage; in the prospective research the asymptomatic initial breast cancer was diagnosed 19 times more frequent than among practically healthy women, endometrial cancer 6 times, and ovarian cancer 1.3 times more frequently than among healthy women.
asymptomatic initial breast cancer is detected in 1,9% and asymptomatic endometrial cancer is detected in only 2,4%, while ovarian cancer is detected only in 1,3% of the patients.

asymptomatic initial polyneoplasias are detected in 5% of primary patients of breast and corpus uteri cancer, and the risk of developing polyneoplasies in patients of breast and endometrium is 10-20 times higher than in healthy women.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the risk of synchronous breast cancer in patients of primary corpus cancer is higher and the risk of endometrial cancer and ovarian cancer in patients of the primary breast cancer is higher than the risk of these neoplasms in the general population.
in the first stage the cumulative risk of polyneoplasty is 2.4 times higher than in patients of the 2.nd stage and 3.5 times higher than in asymptomatic patients.

in primary breast cancer patients of the 1st stage the cumulative risk of corpus uteri cancer development is 13.90 times higher than that in the general population, and in corpus uteri cancer - of breast cancer 8.96.
